title: Generic Type Inference and Compatibility
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of generic type inference and compatibility and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—target typing—in a small, readable example.
Predict the example result and check it against the stated output or a boundary-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study generic type inference and compatibility with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you express type relationships so the compiler can prevent invalid combinations. In this lesson, focus on target typing and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Generics express relationships between types so the compiler can catch many mistakes before runtime. Bounds and wildcards express different constraints; type erasure means generic type arguments are not generally reified at runtime. Apply that reasoning specifically to target typing and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

items.title: Diamond operator
items.text: Operator precedence and numeric promotion determine the resulting value. Make conversions explicit when narrowing a type, and test integer boundaries and floating-point rounding instead of assuming arithmetic is exact.

items.title: Type inference during method invocation
items.text: A method gives a named contract to a unit of behavior. Keep responsibilities focused, define clear parameter and return types, and test typical, boundary, and invalid cases independently.

items.title: Debugging confusing generic compiler errors
items.text: Generics move many type errors to compile time and remove repeated casts. Bounds constrain valid types; wildcards express variance, and Java implements generics through type erasure.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep one clear hypothesis per experiment. Check the version, read the error message, test boundaries, and record what evidence supports your conclusion.
